title: Traffic-replay simulator and counterfactual analyzer for safe batching+cache tuning
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a traffic-replay simulator and counterfactual analysis pipeline that lets us predict cost and latency impacts of batching and KV cache config changes before any production rollout. The tool will produce per-route and per-customer estimates, generate AB test assignments, and wire up dashboards and automated rollback thresholds for safe incremental apply of config changes.
background: Previous AB test tickets focused on live canary experiments and ad-hoc smoke metrics. Those run directly on production traffic and require manual review. For many routes we can reduce risk and accelerate experimentation by first replaying historical traffic under proposed config changes and producing counterfactual metrics (expected cost delta, latency tail regressions, cache hit rate). This ticket formalizes a simulator + analyzer and integrates it into the rollout pipeline so that only simulator-approved configs progress to canary.
proposal: 1) Create a traffic replay component that ingests anonymized request traces and replays requests through the inference runtime sandbox with configurable batching and KV cache settings. 2) Build a counterfactual analyzer that computes cost-per-inference, effective batching factor, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, and cache hit/miss breakdowns for baseline vs candidate configs. 3) Add a scoring step that emits a pass/fail plus confidence intervals and suggested canary sizes. 4) Surface results in a new dashboard and gate the automated rollout pipeline so that only simulator-passed configs are eligible for live canary.
experiment_plan:
- Dataset: last 14 days of anonymized request traces, stratified by route and customer tier.
- Candidate configs: a set of batching window sizes, max_batch_size, batching timeout, kv_cache mode (off/partial/full) and retention TTLs.
- Replay: deterministic replay preserving arrival timestamps and sequence lengths; allow synthetic concentration tests for extreme tails.
- Analysis window: compute metrics aggregated by route and 95% CI using bootstrap.
- Pass criteria: expected cost decrease >= 5% and expected p99 latency regression <= 2% (relative), and cache hit rate change consistent with model.
- If confidence intervals overlap thresholds, simulator will recommend a small canary instead of blocking.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest and replay 14 days of anonymized traces for a test subset of routes within 6 hours.
Counterfactual analyzer produces a report with cost delta, p99 latency delta, cache hit breakdown and a pass/fail recommendation for 90% of candidate configs without manual tuning.
Dashboard panels for top-20 routes show baseline vs candidate comparison and provide CI bands.
Rollout pipeline is gated: a simulator-passed config is automatically eligible to create a 0.5% canary job with suggested canary size and rollback triggers.

Automated rollback triggers are enforced in canary: if p99 latency increases by >5ms absolute or cost increases by >10% over baseline, canary is rolled back automatically and incident note is created.
implementation_notes:
- Reuse existing trace collection (privacy redaction + token hashes).
- Sandbox will run on dedicated smaller cluster to avoid affecting production runtime kernels.
- Use deterministic seed for batching scheduling in the simulator to ensure repeatability.
- Leverage existing metric extraction code from experiments framework for consistent naming.
- Bake in 'stress replay' mode that increases arrival rates to validate autoscaling interplay.
rollout_strategy: 1) MVP internal-only simulator for 10 pilot routes and 3 internal customers. 2) Run daily replay job and produce recommendations; engineering/PM review for first 2 weeks. 3) If results are stable, enable automated gating to create canaries for simulator-passed configs. 4) Expand to top-200 routes over next quarter.
analysis_steps:
- Run simulator for baseline and each candidate config.
- Compute paired differences per-request where possible and aggregate by route.
- Bootstrap to compute 95% CI for cost and p99.
- Use sequential Bayesian test to estimate probability of regression for live canary recommendations.
- Produce a short human-readable summary with numeric deltas and recommended canary size.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: replay doesn't capture cross-request timing effects (KV cache lifecycle). Mitigation: include warmup windows and artificially extend session windows in replay.
- Risk: simulator underestimates tail because of insufficient trace volume. Mitigation: require minimum sample counts and fall back to progressive canary.
- Risk: privacy concerns with traces. Mitigation: strict token hashing, PII redaction, and audit logs for replay jobs.
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to the simulator + analyzer + dashboard gating. Actual live canary orchestration changes will be a follow-up ticket that reads the simulator pass/fail artifact. If the simulator proves effective we will incorporate generated sample size suggestions into the rollout automation.
qa_checklist: Replay preserves request order and sequence IDs
Simulator logs include mismatch summaries between baseline and candidate execution paths
Dashboards show CI bands and link to the raw replay job for debugging
Canary gating honors simulator recommendations and logs human overrides
